en.short_description: Your morning briefing: news, weather, air quality and your stock watchlist.
en.description:
Daily Pulse puts the things you check every morning on one screen, then lets you shape the rest.

—— The morning dashboard ——

A greeting, live weather and air quality for your city (typed in, or found from your location when you ask), the stock watchlist you build, and the day's top stories. One scroll instead of four apps.

—— Feeds that respect your mood ——

GOOD NEWS
Articles scored as positive by sentiment analysis. A real feed, not a gimmick — some mornings you want the news without the dread.

ALERTS
The opposite filter: critical and negative-sentiment breaking stories, when you do want to know.

WORLD NEWS
Global headlines, plus each country's own edition for nine countries, with hashtag filtering.

MY FEED
Shaped by the interests you choose, and editable any time in your profile.

—— Pages you create by asking ——

Tell the built-in assistant what you want and it builds the page, listed on your home screen:

• "Add a crypto page" — a crypto news page
• "Add local news for Tokyo" — a geo-scoped news page
• "What's the weather?" — live conditions for your city
• "Give me today's briefing" — a location and weather summary

The assistant runs on a rule-based engine on your device. It does not send your conversation to an external AI service.

—— Twelve languages ——

English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Hindi, Japanese, Korean and Chinese.

—— Where the data comes from ——

Weather and air quality from Open-Meteo, stock quotes from Yahoo Finance, crypto from CoinGecko, and headlines from public news feeds, each credited to its publisher. Named openly, because you should know what your morning briefing is built on.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
Daily Pulse puts the things you check every morning on one screen, then lets you shape the rest.

Intended audience:
News, weather, air & markets

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
On first launch the app shows a short onboarding (name, city, interests, assistant style; every field can be left blank). It is shown once. The app then opens on a sign-in screen. Sign in with the demo account below, with Sign in with Apple, or with "Continue as guest", which creates an anonymous account with our backend (Supabase) and needs a network connection. After sign-in: Home shows weather and air quality for the city you set (Profile > Location; "Use my current location" there asks for location permission), your stock watchlist (editable in Profile), the Good News and Alerts feeds, and links to World News, My Feed and any page the assistant builds. The assistant opens from the button on Home; try "Add a crypto page" or "Add local news for Tokyo".

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- Supabase — sign-in accounts (email, Apple, or anonymous guest)
- Sign in with Apple — authentication
- Google Sign-In — authentication on Android; the button is not shown on iOS
- Firebase Crashlytics, Analytics, Performance Monitoring and Remote Config
- Device location — only when the user taps "Use my current location"; the position is sent once to OpenStreetMap Nominatim to find the city name and is not stored
- Open-Meteo (weather, air quality), CoinGecko (crypto prices), Yahoo Finance (stock quotes)
- Public news RSS feeds, Google News and Bing News RSS (headlines and search), DuckDuckGo (person summaries)

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app ships 12 languages (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish). Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry. It displays third-party news content: headlines, short summaries and images from publishers' public RSS feeds and from Google News and Bing News, each labelled with its source, with the full article opened at the publisher's own site. Person pages show public DuckDuckGo summaries. No content is licensed or republished in full. The app's artwork, interface and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
Account deletion is available in the app under Profile > Account > Delete Account, and on the support site.
